title: x-temporal
description: The x-temporal extension on an api-spec.yaml operation: the Temporal actions one HTTP call dispatches (triggers) and how their outcomes combine into one response (returnStrategy). Validated at startup by spec.Load (internal/spec/validation.go) and temporal.ValidateBindings. String values may use ${VAR} / ${VAR:-default}, expanded before parsing (ADR-011). Unknown keys are ignored by the gateway; this schema rejects them to catch typos. See ADR-001, ADR-002.

returnStrategy.description: How a multi-trigger operation's HTTP response is derived from its triggers' outcomes. acceptPartial: a genuine mix is 207 Multi-Status, a uniform outcome gets an ordinary status. allOrNothing: anything short of every trigger succeeding is 409 Conflict. No effect on a single-trigger operation (ADR-002).

triggers.description: The Temporal actions this operation dispatches, concurrently. Every trigger is dispatched even if another fails.

action.description: Which Temporal call this trigger makes.

namespace.description: The temporal.connections entry in config.yml this trigger targets. Never inferred; checked against config.yml at startup (ADR-003).

workflowId.description: The target workflow ID. The only templated field: {path.X}, {query.X}, {header.X}, {body.a.b[0]}, {uuidv7}, {fingerprint(ref)}. Placeholders are checked at startup; one a request can't satisfy fails that request with 422 (ADR-004, ADR-020, ADR-025).

signalName.description: signalWorkflow: the signal to send. The request body is its input.

queryType.description: queryWorkflow: the query to run. The request body, if any, is its argument; the result is returned as-is.

workflowType.description: startWorkflow: the workflow type to start. The request body, if any, is its input.

taskQueue.description: startWorkflow: the task queue. Optional when the namespace's temporal.connections[].workflows entry in config.yml declares one for workflowType; an explicit value always wins (ADR-031). Neither fails startup.

idReusePolicy.description: startWorkflow: Temporal's WorkflowIdReusePolicy. TerminateIfRunning is mapped to AllowDuplicate + conflict policy TerminateExisting, so it can't be combined with workflowIdConflictPolicy (ADR-006).

workflowIdConflictPolicy.description: startWorkflow: Temporal's WorkflowIdConflictPolicy, for when a run with this ID is already running.

workflowExecutionErrorWhenAlreadyStarted.description: startWorkflow: return an error instead of attaching to an existing run.

workflowExecutionTimeout.description: startWorkflow: total time across retries and continue-as-new.

workflowRunTimeout.description: startWorkflow: time for a single run.

workflowTaskTimeout.description: startWorkflow: time for a single workflow task.

startDelay.description: startWorkflow: delay before the first workflow task. Can't be combined with cronSchedule.

cronSchedule.description: startWorkflow: cron schedule for a recurring workflow. Can't be combined with startDelay.

memo.description: startWorkflow: memo attached to the run, sent as-is. Not templated: "{...}" text is sent literally.

searchAttributes.description: startWorkflow: typed search attributes. Each value must match its declared type (ADR-007).

enableEagerStart.description: startWorkflow: request eager execution on a local worker.

staticSummary.description: startWorkflow: single-line summary shown in the Temporal UI.

staticDetails.description: startWorkflow: longer details shown in the Temporal UI.

duration.description: A Go duration string, parsed with time.ParseDuration: e.g. "30s", "5m", "1h30m", "500ms".

name.description: The search attribute's name, registered on the Temporal server with a matching type.
